title: Anisotropic Noise Fingerprints Reveal Concept Choice in Concept-Aware Embedding Privacy

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to show that concept-aware anisotropic noise leaks which privacy concept was selected under multi-release access. No prior paper explicitly establishes this relationship or investigates the privacy leakage of concept-aware anisotropic noise under multi-release access. While [12] discusses privacy risks for anisotropic Langevin dynamics, it does not address multi-release access or concept-aware leakage. Similarly, [16] explores attack-aware noise calibration for differential privacy but does not focus on concept-aware anisotropic noise or multi-release access. None of the prior papers substantively match this purpose.

### Mechanism
The mechanism involves a variance fingerprint attack: observing multiple sanitized releases of the same document, differencing them to cancel the embedding and expose noise, computing a per-dimension variance profile from squared differences, and matching it to normalized concept covariance templates via minimum Euclidean distance. [14] discusses statistical log differencing, which involves differencing logs to model their differences, but it does not compute variance profiles or match them to concept covariance templates. [25] addresses covariance estimation in image classification but does not involve differencing multiple releases or matching to templates. No prior paper implements a substantively equivalent mechanism.

### Evaluation
The evaluation uses SPARSE-style sanitization (GTR-T5-Base, K=5 concepts, N=10 releases) to achieve 100% concept-identification accuracy vs 18.9% for isotropic noise. [12] evaluates privacy risks for anisotropic Langevin dynamics but does not use SPARSE-style sanitization or multi-release setups. [16] evaluates attack-aware noise calibration but does not involve concept identification or SPARSE-style sanitization. No prior paper uses the same evaluation design, making this facet uncovered.

### Domain
The domain is embedding privacy/differential privacy for embeddings (RAG, vector databases). [15] and [23] address differential privacy mechanisms, and [10] evaluates differential privacy in federated learning, all within the general area of embedding privacy. While none of these papers target the specific sub-problem of concept-aware anisotropic noise leakage under multi-release access, they operate in the same general application area. Thus, the domain is covered.
